name: Nogai
variety: Literary Nogai of the North Caucasus (Dagestan, Karachay-Cherkessia, Stavropol), Cyrillic script
sources: Csató, Éva Á. & Karakoç, Birsel (1998). Noghay. In Lars Johanson & Éva Á. Csató (eds.), The Turkic Languages. Routledge.
Baskakov, N. A. (1940). Nogajskij jazyk i ego dialekty: grammatika, teksty i slovar'. Izdatel'stvo Akademii Nauk SSSR.
contrasts: nine vowels: front /i y e ø æ/ and back /ɯ u o ɑ/, the front rounded and open front vowels spelt with digraphs (уь, оь, аь)
velar /k ɡ/ versus uvular /q ʁ/, tied to vowel backness in native words
sibilant shift typical of the Kipchak-Nogai group: /ʃ/ where most Turkic languages have /tʃ/ and /s/ where they have /ʃ/ (уьш 'three', бес 'five', тас 'stone')
allophony: к and г are uvular [q] and [ʁ] next to back vowels, velar next to front vowels
/l/ is velarised next to back vowels
в is [w] in native words and [v] in Russian loans
suffix-initial consonants assimilate to the end of the stem (plural -лар, -лер, -нар, -нер)
/f v ts tʃ/ occur in Russian loans only
phonotactics: no onset clusters in native words
coda clusters are sonorant + obstruent (доьрт, кырк)
backness harmony in native words and suffixes; rounding harmony is weak and not written beyond the first syllable
/ŋ/ (spelt нъ) does not begin a word
ь and ъ are parts of the digraphs аь, оь, уь, нъ; elsewhere they belong to Russian spelling

stress.type: fixed final by default, with morphological exceptions
stress.rule: Stress falls on the last syllable of the word; predicative personal endings, the negative suffix and the question particle are unstressed and leave the stress on the syllable before them.
stress.cues: not instrumentally studied in the sources used

rhythm.vowel_reduction: moderate: the high vowels are short and lax and may be dropped in fast speech, as in the closely related Kazakh and Karakalpak
rhythm.notes: Low confidence: no instrumental study of Nogai timing was available to me.

length.notes: No vowel length contrast. Geminates occur at morpheme boundaries and in a few stems.

intonation.declarative: rise at the end of non-final phrases, fall at the end of the statement
intonation.yes_no_question: marked by the particle ма/ме (ба/бе, па/пе); pitch is high before the particle
intonation.wh_question: prominence on the question word, final fall
intonation.continuation: rise at the end of non-final phrases
intonation.accent_shape: rise to a high on the final stressed syllable
intonation.notes: Low confidence: no instrumental study of Nogai intonation was available to me; the entries follow the general pattern of the better described Turkic languages (Turkish, Kazakh).

problems: the phoneme table is the Kazakh one without changes; the mid vowel оь (/ø/) has the short duration of the high vowels (100 against 200)
outside the digraphs, ь and ъ are read as glottal stops (кельди, альбом, объект)
the rule for the past copula еди stresses the penultimate syllable of every word ending in -еди (келеди, келмеди)
the clear l chosen by the rules is turned into dark [ɫ] by the Kazakh phoneme table whenever no front vowel follows (эл, бел, кел-)
Russian loanwords need the _^_RU mark in the word list, which has only three such entries
t is the unaspirated base2 stop while p and k use aspirated samples
good: final stress is written into the rules, with the personal endings and the question particle unstressed (бараман, бармайман)
к and г choose velar or uvular variants by vowel class; нъ is [ŋ]; аь, оь, уь are front vowels
в is [w] next to back vowels; word-initial е is [je]
vowel harmony follows from the spelling

notes: The voice is marked 'status testing' in eSpeak NG. The consonant list includes /f v ts tʃ/, which occur in loanwords only. The degree of aspiration of the voiceless stops is not documented in the sources used.
